text:
Kenji: Quick spike idea — propose an 'inflight attribution proxy' that tags requests with billing keys / tenant context before enrichment. Trying to reduce late-joiner lookups and make cost attribution available in downstream samplers.
Miriam: short summary pls? I'm picturing another proxy service. latency concerns?
Kenji: yep. Two sketches:
1) inline proxy — placed in front of ingest, does cheap header resolution & canonicalization synchronously, forwards enriched envelope.
2) async adorner — accept raw envelope, enqueue fast attach job that races, downstream consumers merge when ready (graceful fallback to lookup)
Jordan: tradeoff: inline adds ~1-5ms p99 if we do k-v lookup sync. But it guarantees attribution for sampling and early metrics. Async reduces latency at the cost of more complex joins and potential missing keys.
Sara: Important: must ensure idempotency — if proxy retries we can't double-count. Also how does this interact with sampling? If key missing, we need deterministic fallback so samples aren't biased.
Kenji: Agreed. For inline we use local cache + async refresh; fallback to 'unattributed' tag with stable sentinel. For async adorner we add an 'adorn_state' bit to envelope and a merge TTL.
Miriam: What about cardinality explosion? If we attach full billing metadata early we might blow up cardinality in metrics/ingest.
Kenji: plan is to attach only a compact billing key (sha256 short) + tenant tier tag; full resolution happens only on demand in analytics path. This keeps ingest envelope small.
Jordan: also consider backpressure — proxy needs a small memcache and bounded concurrency to avoid becoming single-point-of-failure.
Sara: ops: how do we rollout? Canary the inline proxy in front of a low-traffic ingress, compare attribution rates and latency. If success, roll more.
Kenji: +1. I'll draft an RFC with diagrams and perf targets. Devops, please add SLO for proxy p95 latency <= 10ms and error budget mapping.
devbot: deployment note: canary env created (canary/proxy-attrib-001) :rocket:
Miriam: Also add tests for sampling parity and end-to-end cost tally. We don't want hidden accounting diffs.
Kenji: Thanks — will post RFC link when ready. /cc @sara @jordan
